query: Identify a processing route and property optimization strategy for a lightweight, multi-principal element alloy system. The goal is to achieve high density and hardness while ensuring resistance to high-temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion. Request a hypothesis for the material composition and processing method, supporting evidence on phase stability, boundary conditions for the processing temperature, and a falsification experiment to test the mechanism of property enhancement.

generation.hypothesis: Processing an Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 high-entropy alloy via severe surface deformation (Stationary Friction Processing) to achieve an ultrafine-grain microstructure will simultaneously enhance hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance by promoting the formation of a dense, protective Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale, while maintaining aqueous corrosion resistance through compositional homogeneity.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 high-entropy alloy with coarse grain structure (approx. 98 μm) containing BCC/B2 phases.
generation.intervention: Severe surface deformation using Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) at controlled temperatures (e.g., 400°C or 1800°C equivalent strain) to refine grains to ultrafine/nanocrystalline scale (1 μm or 0.43 μm).
generation.conditions: Processing temperature range: 400°C to 1800°C (strain rate dependent); Oxidation testing at 900-1100°C; Aqueous corrosion testing in neutral/sulfuric acid environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grain microstructure with high grain boundary density and enhanced elemental homogeneity.
generation.mechanism: High grain boundary density accelerates diffusion of Al and Cr to the surface, facilitating rapid formation of a continuous, dense, and adherent Al2O3/Cr2O3 oxide scale that acts as a barrier against oxygen ingress and ion diffusion, thereby reducing oxidation kinetics. The refined microstructure also impedes dislocation motion, increasing hardness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Vickers hardness increase to >600 Hv; Oxidation mass gain reduction by >50% compared to as-cast at 1000°C; Retained corrosion resistance in H2SO4 solution.
generation.baseline: As-cast Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 alloy with coarse grains and lower hardness (~300-400 Hv) and higher oxidation mass gain.
generation.boundary: Processing temperature must not exceed the melting point or cause excessive grain coarsening (>1400°C may lead to Laves phase precipitation and grain growth, degrading properties).
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal SFP temperature and strain rate for balancing hardness and oxidation resistance may vary; long-term stability of the ultrafine grain structure at extreme temperatures (>1200°C) is not fully characterized.
generation.falsification_experiment: Perform SFP on Al0.2Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2 at a temperature known to cause grain coarsening (e.g., >1400°C) and compare oxidation mass gain and hardness to the ultrafine-grained sample. If the coarsened sample shows equal or better oxidation resistance and hardness, the mechanism of grain-boundary-enhanced diffusion is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In this paper, the impact of mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS) on the phase evolution and mechanical properties development of CoCrFeNiTi high–entropy alloys (HEAs) was investigated. The microstructure and properties of the material were examined, using X-ray diffraction (XRD) for phase identification, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for surface morphology observation, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) for microstructural analysis, and hardness testing to evaluate mechanical performance. The milled powder exhibited nanocrystalline solid solution microstructure with grain sizes below 48 nm, composed of 83% face–centered cubic (FCC) and 17% body–centered cubic (BCC) phases. Mechanically, the bulk CoCrFeNiTi alloy exhibited exceptional strength attributes, as evidenced by a Vickers hardness value reaching 675 Hv, along with a compressive strength of 1894 MPa and a yield stress of 1238 MPa.
